summary.text: The cover of the English November 2019 WHO policy brief recommending social network-based HIV testing for key populations as part of partner services.

blocks.title: Page 2
blocks.content:
WHO recommends social network-based HIV testing approaches for key populations as part of partner services package
The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends 
voluntary HIV testing services (HTS) for sexual and drug-
injecting partners of all people with HIV. An effective 
approach is provider-assisted referral when a trained 
provider offers voluntary HTS to partner(s) with the 
consent of HIV-positive client. Provider-assisted referral is 
a safe and effective strategy for identifying additional HIV 
infections and prioritizing prevention services for partners 
who are vulnerable to HIV

summary.text: Explains that WHO recommends voluntary testing for the sexual and drug-injecting partners of people with HIV, but that key populations often fear stigma and breaches of confidentiality when naming partners. It defines social network-based testing, summarises review findings on its benefits and safety, and states the new recommendation.

blocks.title: Page 3
blocks.content:
Several promising models for social network-based 
approaches have emerged that can be considered. These 
include: 
•	 use of peers to recruit key populations in their networks 
for HTS; 
•	 distribution of HIV self-testing kits by HIV-positive and 
HIV-negative clients to their partners and contacts;
•	 use of new tools and technologies, such as digital 
and social media, text messaging and other web-based 
platforms, to reach social networks, especially for young 
key populations; 
•	 use of anonymous methods for partner services 
and social network-based approaches to protect

summary.text: Lists promising social network-based testing models and the operational principles of confidentiality, voluntariness and differentiated service choice. It gives LINKAGES project examples from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Haiti and Malawi showing high HIV-positive yields among tested contacts.

social network-based approaches where appropriate, at

summary.text: Recommends offering partner services to newly diagnosed key population members at diagnosis and periodically, and weighing limited-wave versus ongoing network approaches. It addresses client safety and the need for monitoring indicators and reviewing programmes when harms occur, and includes WHO contact and licence details.
